```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(
  collapse = TRUE,
  comment = "#>",
  eval = requireNamespace("pharmaversesdtm", quietly = TRUE)
)
```

Clinical datasets carry identifiers, dates and product names that should not
leave your environment, yet an AI agent helps most when it can see the real
structure of the data: which domains exist, which variables they hold and what
typical records look like. This article anonymizes five SDTM domains from
[pharmaversesdtm](https://pharmaverse.github.io/pharmaversesdtm/) and produces
two files:

- a Markdown file describing the data, safe to paste into a prompt or hand to
  an agent, and
- an `.RData` file holding the anonymized datasets, for an agent or colleague
  who needs to run code against them.

Both files come from the same anonymized copy of the data, so the description
matches the datasets exactly.

```{r packages}
library(anon)
library(pharmaversesdtm)

sdtm <- list(dm = dm, ex = ex, pc = pc, lb = lb, vs = vs)
```

## What needs protecting

| Information | Variables | Treatment |
|---|---|---|
| Study identifier | `STUDYID` and any text containing it | Replace with `STUDY01` |
| Subject identifiers | `USUBJID`, `SUBJID` | Pseudonyms, consistent across domains |
| Site | `SITEID` | Pseudonyms |
| Dates | every `--DTC` variable | Shift by one study-wide offset |
| Date of birth | `BRTHDTC` | Remove |
| Age | `AGE` | Cap at 90 |
| Product and vendor names | `EXTRT`, `PCTEST`, `ARM`, `PCNAM`, ... | Replace by pattern |

Two choices keep the anonymized data useful:

- **Subject pseudonyms are built once for all domains.** Applying a sequence
  function to each dataset separately would give the same subject different
  IDs in `dm` and `pc`, and the domains could no longer be joined.
- **All dates move by the same number of days.** Study days, time since dose
  and visit windows stay correct, while calendar dates no longer identify
  anyone.

## Build the lookups

```{r lookups}
set.seed(2024)

subjects <- sort(unique(unlist(lapply(sdtm, `[[`, "USUBJID"))))
subject_key <- setNames(
  anon_id_chr_sequence(subjects, scramble = TRUE, start = "SUBJ-"),
  subjects
)

subjid_key <- setNames(sub("^SUBJ-", "", subject_key[dm$USUBJID]), dm$SUBJID)

sites <- sort(unique(dm$SITEID))
site_key <- setNames(
  anon_id_chr_sequence(sites, scramble = TRUE, start = "SITE-"),
  sites
)

date_offset <- -sample(365:1095, 1)
```

The seed makes this article reproducible. For real data, don't fix the seed,
and keep `subject_key`, `site_key` and `date_offset` out of anything you share:
they are what links the anonymized data back to the source.

SDTM dates are ISO 8601 strings with varying precision. `anon_date_shift()`
with a fixed `offset` moves each one by exactly that many days and returns it
in the same format: any time part is kept, and a partial date such as
`2014-03` keeps its precision.

```{r shift-dtc}
anon_date_shift(
  c("2014-01-02", "2014-01-02T08:30", "2014-03", ""),
  offset = date_offset
)
```

## Set the rules as global options

Global options apply to every later `anon()` call, so the same rules protect
each domain without repeating them. `pattern_list` replaces text wherever it
appears, including in labels; `df_variable_names` replaces whole columns by
name, either with a fixed value or with a function of the column.

```{r options}
dtc_vars <- grep("DTC$", unique(unlist(lapply(sdtm, names))), value = TRUE)
dtc_vars <- setdiff(dtc_vars, "BRTHDTC")
dtc_vars

dtc_rules <- setNames(
  rep(list(~ anon_date_shift(.x, offset = date_offset)), length(dtc_vars)),
  dtc_vars
)

old_options <- anon_options(
  pattern_list = list(
    STUDY01 = "CDISCPILOT01",
    DRUG = c("Xanomeline", "\\bXAN\\b", "Xan(?=_)"),
    "[LAB]" = "Imaginary Labs"
  ),
  df_variable_names = c(
    list(
      USUBJID = ~ unname(subject_key[.x]),
      SUBJID = ~ unname(subjid_key[.x]),
      SITEID = ~ unname(site_key[.x]),
      AGE = ~ pmin(.x, 90),
      BRTHDTC = ""
    ),
    dtc_rules
  )
)
```

`anon_options()` returns the previous values, so they can be restored later
with `options(old_options)`.

## Anonymize the domains

```{r anonymize}
anon_sdtm <- unclass(anon(sdtm))

head(anon_sdtm$dm[, c("STUDYID", "USUBJID", "SUBJID", "SITEID", "RFSTDTC",
                      "BRTHDTC", "AGE", "ARM")], 3)
head(anon_sdtm$pc[, c("USUBJID", "PCTESTCD", "PCTEST", "PCNAM", "PCDTC")], 3)
```

The anonymized domains still join on `USUBJID`, and the time between dose and
sample is unchanged:

```{r checks}
all(anon_sdtm$pc$USUBJID %in% anon_sdtm$dm$USUBJID)

unique(
  as.Date(substr(anon_sdtm$pc$PCDTC, 1, 10)) - as.Date(substr(pc$PCDTC, 1, 10))
)
```

A quick check that none of the source identifiers or names remain:

```{r leak-check}
sensitive <- c(subjects, "CDISCPILOT01", "Xanomeline", "Imaginary Labs",
               dm$BRTHDTC)
shared_text <- unlist(lapply(anon_sdtm, function(df) {
  unlist(lapply(df[vapply(df, is.character, logical(1))], unique))
}))
any(shared_text %in% sensitive)
any(grepl("xanomeline|cdiscpilot|imaginary", shared_text, ignore.case = TRUE))
```

## Write the files to share

The rules have done their job, so restore the previous options before building
the report. The report then describes the anonymized data as it is; applying
the rules a second time would shift the dates again and fail to look up
subject IDs that are already pseudonyms.

```{r restore}
options(old_options)
```

```{r outputs}
out_dir <- file.path(tempdir(), "sdtm-anon")
dir.create(out_dir, showWarnings = FALSE)

report <- anon_report(
  anon_sdtm,
  example_values_n = 3,
  example_rows = anon_example_rows(n = 3, key = "USUBJID", method = "first")
)

context_file <- file.path(out_dir, "sdtm-context.md")
writeLines(
  anon_prompt_bundle(
    report = report,
    format = "markdown",
    title = "Anonymized SDTM domains: dm, ex, pc, lb, vs"
  ),
  context_file
)

rdata_file <- file.path(out_dir, "sdtm-anon.RData")
anon_env <- list2env(anon_sdtm)
save(list = names(anon_sdtm), envir = anon_env, file = rdata_file)

basename(list.files(out_dir))
```

`sdtm-context.md` lists each domain with its variables, missingness and a few
example values, plus example records for one subject across every domain.
Here is its start:

```{r preview, echo = FALSE, comment = ""}
cat(head(readLines(context_file), 40), sep = "\n")
```

Loading `sdtm-anon.RData` restores the five anonymized domains under their
original names:

```{r load}
check_env <- new.env()
load(rdata_file, envir = check_env)
ls(check_env)
nrow(check_env$pc)
```

## Before you share

- Review the Markdown file once before sending it. The rules cover the
  variables listed above; free-text variables such as comments
  (`--ORRES` text, `CO` domain) need their own rules or NLP redaction with
  `nlp_auto()`.
- Keep the lookups and the date offset private, and don't save them in the
  `.RData` file.
- `anon_report()` also applies the global rules to its example values and
  rows, so `anon_report(sdtm)` with the options still set is safe too. Building
  it from the anonymized copy, as here, guarantees the Markdown file describes
  exactly what is in the `.RData` file.
